subject: Admin activity: live stream vs batch export options and redaction scenarios
messages:
From: Elaine Torres <elaine@medisphere.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medisphere.com
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Admin activity - evidence extraction options and questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for taking this call earlier. For our SOC 2 and SIG review we need definitive answers on what admin activity is recorded and how it can be exported. A few specific items the audit team asked for: 

- Live streaming vs batch snapshots: can you push a live audit stream (Kafka/HTTP) or only provide periodic snapshots? If both, what fields differ in the live stream vs the snapshot?
- Field-level redaction: we need tenant-scoped PII removed on export (customer email, user_display_name) but preserved in operator-trail for internal debugging. Is pseudonymization supported at export time?
- Time zone normalization: timestamps should be normalized to UTC and include original timezone if available.
- Signed manifests: we need a chain-of-custody proof — per-file checksum + per-record hash salted with a tenant-specific nonce. Is there tooling to verify?
- Retention windows by event class (admin, operator, system): what can you commit to and how easy is it to get a historical range?

Also the procurement team wants an estimate for how long an on-demand full export (30 days of admin events for a single tenant) would take and whether there are charges.

Could you send a short proposal and attach a sample manifest so our auditors can vet the format?

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Torres
Security Engineer, Medisphere Health

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Torres <elaine@medisphere.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity - evidence extraction options and questions

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Below is a succinct summary of our options and what we recommend for a SOC 2/SIG handoff. Attaching: export_spec_v2.xlsx (fields matrix) and signed_manifest_sample.json.

1) Live stream (recommended for near-real-time monitoring)
   - Protocols: HTTPS push (webhook) or we can stream to a customer-owned Kafka endpoint.
   - Contents: each live event includes: event_id, event_type, actor_id (internal id), actor_email (can be redacted), target_resource, action, timestamp_utc, region, request_id, raw_payload (only for system events).
   - Differences vs snapshot: live stream omits some internal-only debug fields (kernel_trace) and is single-event; snapshots include full context and linked session fragments.

2) Batch snapshot (recommended for attestations and archival handoff)
   - Delivery: S3 push, SFTP, or signed HTTPS bundle.
   - Format: newline-delimited JSON with per-record SHA256, file-level signed manifest (Ed25519), and an optional per-record HMAC with a tenant nonce.

3) Redaction & pseudonymization
   - Export-time transforms supported: remove, mask, hash (sha256), or replace with stable pseudonym.
   - We can apply tenant-specific nonce-based hashing for actor_email and user_display_name on exports; original values remain in internal operator trails only.

4) Time zone and timestamp policy
   - All emitted timestamps are normalized to UTC (ISO8601). We include original tz offset in an optional field: original_timestamp.

5) Retention and historical pulls
   - Default retention: admin events 365 days, operator/privileged actions 540 days for Dedicated/Enterprise customers (configurable under Private).
   - On-demand pulls: small ranges (<=7 days) delivered within 1 business day; 30-day full tenant snapshot: typical turnaround 3-5 business days for SFTP/S3 delivery.

6) Chain-of-custody verification
   - We produce: file-level Ed25519 signature, file SHA256 checksum, and per-record SHA256 salted with tenant nonce. We can provide verification tooling (Python scripts) and a simple manifest verifier.

7) Pricing note
   - On-demand archival exports are billable beyond the included entitlement; procurement will get a quote once scope and frequency are confirmed.

Next steps: If you want the signed SFTP snapshot workflow, confirm the target path and whether you want per-record pseudonymization or redaction. I'll loop in Ben for the export SLA commit and Kim for documentation and verification tooling.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, Elaine Torres <elaine@medisphere.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity - evidence extraction options and questions

Quick technical notes from the runtime side:

- Event classes: we tag events as admin_action, operator_action, system_event, api_access. The binary payloads for system_event are stored separately and not included in default snapshots unless explicitly requested.
- Per-record hashing: we compute SHA256 over a canonicalized JSON of the record + tenant_nonce and output hex digest in the manifest. We rotate the tenant_nonce on request (audit-only) and will re-hash existing exports if you require re-attestation — note this is a manual job.
- Redaction latency: pseudonymization at export time is performed in-stream and doesn't materially delay small exports. For full snapshots we run a parallel redaction pass — add 6-12 hours for very large date ranges.
- On-demand SLA: 1 business day for <=7 days; 3 business days for 8-30 days; >30 days requires planning (timeline quoted).

I'll add a short README to the signed_manifest_sample.json outlining verification steps. If Medisphere prefers a signed per-record signature (not just hash), we can offer an HSM-backed attestation for an extra compliance fee.

- Ben
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Stephanie / Ben — this is great, thank you. A couple quick clarifications for our auditors: 

- We will request SFTP delivery with per-record pseudonymization (tenant_nonce salted SHA256) and an Ed25519-signed manifest. Please confirm the exact manifest fields you will include.
- Can you include a column in the export_spec_v2.xlsx showing which fields are redacted vs pseudonymized vs kept in plain? (I saw the matrix but auditors prefer a single-column summary.)
- For pricing: procurement wants a one-time fee estimate for the 30-day snapshot and an ongoing monthly estimate if we request weekly 7-day rolling snapshots.

If you can send the manifest template and a short quote, we can route to procurement and our external auditor.

Thanks,
Elaine

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Thanks Elaine — attaching the manifest template and a one-page pricing snapshot. Quick answers: manifest fields we produce: file_name, file_sha256, file_size_bytes, file_signature_ed25519, record_count, tenant_nonce_hash, export_start_utc, export_end_utc, processing_notes. We'll add a summary column to export_spec_v2.xlsx and send a quote for: (a) one-time 30-day SFTP snapshot, (b) recurring weekly 7-day snapshots.

I'll send the formal quote and the manifest template by EOD Pacific. If procurement needs a shorter SLA for delivery we can prioritize for a fee.

Stephanie
